subject: Staged region binding & subprocessor onboarding - DPA annex and timeline
messages:
From: Emily Carter <emily.carter@acmehealth.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com, ops@acmehealth.com
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Staged residency commitment & subprocessor roster - initial ask

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. Acme is moving quickly on the pilot and Procurement needs to clarify a few things before legal signs off on the SOW. High-level asks:

- Can Redwood support staged region binding (i.e., pin by tenant/organization) where we scope EU patient traffic to EU-only first, then expand to US and APAC in later phases?
- For the in-region promise, what is the operational definition (percent of requests that must remain in-region, telemetry to prove it, and acceptable transient failovers)?
- We need a current subprocessor roster and an approximate timeline for approvals and onboarding of any new subprocessors (especially any third-party analytics or monitoring vendors).
- Please share the DPA annex language for transient cross-region processing and a draft addendum if you have one.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a phased acceptance plan and an ops checklist we can include in our procurement playbook? Ideally we’ll lock Phase 1 (EU-only for EU customers) in the contract and have a clear rollout window for the other regions.

If it helps, we can schedule a short call with our DevOps and Privacy teams on Monday.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we’re on a compressed timeline for the pilot start.

Best,
Emily Carter
Head of Procurement, Acme Health

Subject: Re: Staged residency commitment & subprocessor roster - initial ask

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front: yes, Redwood can support a staged, tenant-scoped pinning approach; we can provide a subprocessor roster and a DPA annex draft for your review.

Proposed next steps from our side:
1) Phase plan: we usually do a two-step rollout for accounts with residency constraints — Phase A (EU pin for EU-scoped tenants), Phase B (US+APAC add) with a mutually agreed window. We can commit to an operational target (example: >= 98% in-region by steady state, with documented transient failovers up to 72 hours for certain maintenance/replication events).
2) Ops checklist: I’ll ask Marissa (on Product Ops) to publish an onboarding checklist that calls out telemetry keys, metrics, and the acceptance criteria you can include in the SOW.
3) Legal DPA annex: Kimberly is looping in legal to propose language for transient cross-region processing, audit evidence, and subprocessor controls.

I’ve cc’d Kimberly and Marissa — Kimberly, can you sketch the DPA addendum with language around temporary failover windows, auditability, and KMS handling? Marissa — can you share a draft ops checklist and the current subprocessor roster by EOD Monday?

Emily — if Monday morning works, let’s do a 30-minute call (our calendar: Tue 10–10:30 PT or Mon 11–11:30 PT). Which works on your side?

—Jordan
Jordan Blake

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Carter <emily.carter@acmehealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Staged residency commitment & subprocessor roster - draft DPA addendum

Hi Emily and team,

Thanks Jordan — below is an initial draft summary and items we plan to put into a formal addendum (attached as DPA_Addendum_ACME_v1.pdf). This is a draft for discussion; happy to iterate on language in the call.

Key points we propose including in the DPA addendum:
- Scope & Pinning Model: Redwood will provide tenant-level region binding. The contract will enumerate tenants in Phase A (EU-only) and Phase B (US/APAC). Phase transition requires mutual written acknowledgement.
- Operational Definition: Steady-state in-region coverage target = 98%. Transient cross-region processing is permitted for replication, cache warm-up, and disaster recovery; any transient processing outside the pinned region will be limited to a 72-hour window unless agreed otherwise. All transient events will be logged and surfaced in audit reports.
- Subprocessors: Current roster (attached) plus onboarding cadence. Redwood will notify Acme 30 days before activation of new subprocessors that may process scoped data. For any subprocessor that processes EU personal data outside the EU, Redwood will provide transfer safeguards (SCCs or equivalent) and a technical runbook describing what data is processed and how it is protected.
- KMS & Key Control: For private deployments we support customer-managed KMS; for hosted deployments we offer an option to use dedicated encryption keys per-tenant. Key rotation and access audit logs will be provided on request.
- Auditability & Evidence: Redwood will deliver monthly residency telemetry snapshots for the pilot period and provide on-demand logs for specific incidents. We will include a sample telemetry schema in the addendum.
- Exceptions & Temporary Failover: Any exception >72 hours will trigger escalation to the Customer Success and Security leads and require remediation steps in an agreed runbook.

Attachments included: DPA_Addendum_ACME_v1.pdf (draft clauses, telemetry schema), Subprocessor_Roster_20270529.csv (current roster export).

Open questions for Acme:
- Are there particular subprocessors you need us to treat as approvable (explicit opt-in) vs. generally permitted with notice?
- Do you require SCCs for all non-EEA subprocessors or would a combination of SCCs + documented technical safeguards be sufficient?

Jordan / Marissa — if you can push the ops checklist and the telemetry sample into the shared link before Monday, I’ll incorporate the references into section 3.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com

Jordan / Kimberly / Marissa — thanks for the fast work and the attachments. A few quick notes after an internal read:

- The 98% steady-state target + 72-hour transient window is acceptable for Phase A, provided we can see the monthly telemetry snapshots during the pilot.
- For subprocessors: Acme requires 30-day prior notice for new subprocessors. For any analytics or monitoring vendor that will see identifiers or de-identified health attributes, we will need explicit approval before activation.
- SCCs: We prefer SCCs for non-EEA subprocessors that process EU personal data; if Redwood can provide SCCs + the technical runbook, that will satisfy Legal.

Next steps: please upload the addendum and roster to the HubSpot record and send a DocuSign-ready copy of the addendum (we’ll do signature counters via procurement). Also, Monday 11:00 PT works for a quick call — please send an invite for 30 minutes and include our DevOps lead (ops@acmehealth.com).

Emily Carter
Head of Procurement, Acme Health
